entries.title: one rule says whether a path is a test file
entries.summary: A test directory at the repository root was not a test directory: find_dead_code reported tests/helpers.py dead, and the deletion investigator called a name it imports imported by nothing live. Six rules answered the question and no two agreed. There is one rule now and every tool imports it; check_delete_safe and check_edit_safe read it too, so a production models/pod_spec.py is not a test.

entries.title: an entry point has no importer, and that does not make it dead
entries.summary: The deletion investigator called an importer dead when nothing imported it. An entry point has no importer by construction, so a name imported only by main.py, by the file package.json names, by a package's __init__.py or by a test read as imported by nothing live. The investigator asks find_dead_code, which knows the project's roots, and keeps no answer of its own.

entries.title: the deletion investigator reads the match the search made
entries.summary: The reference search compares import names through one fold, so an import spelled in another Unicode form or with an escape is an import of the plain name. The deletion investigator then filtered those rows again with a raw comparison, lost them, and answered that no file imports a name a live file imports. It reads the match type the search already states and compares no name of its own.

entries.title: a call written with an escape is still a call
entries.summary: A Java, C# or JavaScript call can spell a name with a Unicode escape, and the compiler reads it as the plain name.
